what: The encoder endpoint before and after the one restart of the units for the DESIGN A5 revision before the M1 merge (the encoder unit requires its socket unit; mesa-clm-encoder-proxy instead of systemd-socket-proxyd). Both records were written by scripts/endpoint_checks.py; 'before_restart' held 100 idle connections, 'after_restart' 1,000.

restart.reset_failed_then_restart: systemctl --user reset-failed mesa-clm-encoder.service; systemctl --user restart mesa-clm-encoder.service mesa-clm-serve.service

notes: before: systemd-socket-proxyd under the user manager's soft RLIMIT_NOFILE of 1,024 took six descriptors per connection (100 idle connections: 609 descriptors), so about 170 idle connections exhaust it
after: mesa-clm-encoder-proxy under LimitNOFILE=16384 takes two per connection (1,000 idle connections: 2,009 descriptors) and the endpoint answered a keyed GET /v1/models while they were held

the proxy process recorded here started before the listen-backlog fix of serving/encoder_proxy.py (asyncio's default backlog of 100 on 127.0.0.1:8090, instead of net.core.somaxconn 4096); the installed copy has the fix, which takes effect at the next start of the units

mesa-clm-encoder-proxy.service.ExecStart: { path=/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-socket-proxyd ; argv[]=/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-socket-proxyd ~/.mesa/clm/run/encoder.sock ; ignore_errors=no ; start_time=[n/a] ; stop_time=[n/a] ; pid=0 ; code=(null) ; status=0/0 }
